newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish premier calls for action on child abuse.
newsitem.headline: Polish premier calls for action on child abuse.

text.p: Poland's prime minister called on Wednesday for the creation of a special office to protect children's rights and for police hot lines to combat growing child sex abuse.
Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told legislators, voluntary groups and police in Warsaw that social changes were leading to new threats to the rights of Poland's 12 million children.
"There is therefore an urgent need to act against all forms of violence against children and infringement of their rights," a government information office statement quoted him as saying.
He supported the appointment of a Children's Rights Spokesman -- a state office independent of the administration and judiciary, who would be well-known and easily accessible.
The prime minister told the education ministry to step up programmes to prevent sexual abuse, including training of teachers and effective instruction of children, the statement said.
He also asked the police to examine whether they could adopt from a British model a system of hotlines to police stations, staffed by retired officers.
Polish public opinion has become increasingly aware of and alarmed over abuse of children, especially in households where parents are alcoholics.
Concern has been heightened by several cases involving child prostitution.
There has also been mounting concern over children who come hungry to school, partly because of hardship as market reforms have been accompanied by unemployment above 13 percent.
